MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Job Description:

Better and fairer care. Always.

We are St Vincent's Health Australia, Australia's largest not-for-profit provider of health and aged care services. 

Founded by The Sisters of Charity in 1857, our +30,000 healthcare superheroes operate public and private hospitals, residential aged care, community and virtual care, and outreach programs. 

About the role

Lead and inspire a multidisciplinary administrative team to deliver high-performing, patient-focused outpatient services.

Drive operational excellence through workforce planning, clinic optimisation, and effective management of patient access, waitlists, and referrals.

Harness data, reporting, and performance metrics to support service growth, funding outcomes, and informed decision-making.

Champion continuous improvement initiatives that enhance patient experience, service efficiency, and quality outcomes.

Collaborate with clinical leaders and key stakeholders to implement strategic priorities, lead change, and shape the future of outpatient care.

About you

Demonstrated experience managing outpatient clinic operations within a complex healthcare environment.

Solid understanding of outpatient clinic operations, including electronic patient records and scheduling systems, billing practices, non-admitted patient data, Activity Based Funding (ABF), and staff roster management.

Proven leadership experience in workforce planning, performance management, and developing high-performing teams.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to use data to improve service delivery, patient flow, and operational performance.

Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with a commitment to patient-centred care and continuous improvement.

Why work at St Vincent's?

Salary packaging of up to $15,900 per FBT year (pay less tax and increase your take-home pay), with increased benefits for full-time employees such as reductions to rent or mortgage payments, vehicle leasing, and a meal entertainment card up to $2,600 a year

Discounts including gym memberships through Fitness Passport, health insurance, onsite pharmacy

Options to purchase additional leave in support of work-life balance

Opportunity to join our workplace giving program, Give4Good

About St Vincent's Private Community Hospital Griffith

A modern medical & surgical hospital, 20 In- patient beds and 3 state-of-the-art operating theatre

Established to provide access to excellent health services closer to home for our regional community

Over 85 employees, providing compassionate & professional care for our patients & their families

Onsite training facility, The Murrumbidgee Clinical Teaching and Learning Centre and onsite consulting suites that support the provision of services for our 30 Visiting Medical specialists

Convenient location close to cafes, restaurants, and public transport

Sponsorship - work rights for Australia

Please note, visa sponsorship is not available for this position. For this role you must be an Australian or New Zealand citizen or have an Australia visa that grants you the work rights necessary for the role.

Pre-employment checks

Your employment is conditional upon the completion of all role-required pre-employment checks, including relevant immunisations.

Equal opportunity

We celebrate diversity & inclusion and are committed to equal employment opportunity for everyone.

As part of our commitment to reconciliation, we encourage Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples to apply and join us in delivering care that heals body, mind, spirit and community.

How to apply

The closing date for applications is Midnight, 24th July 2026.

Candidates maybe selected prior to closing date. Hence, please apply soonest.

Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter highlighting how your interest, skills, and experience align with each of the things listed in the About You section of this job advert.

Respectfully, this role is not open to recruitment agencies.

result.description: TOTALYTY PTY LTD  We are seeking an experienced and commercially focused  Marketing Specialist  to join our team.  The Marketing Specialist will identify market opportunities and develop, coordinate and implement marketing strategies for Totalyty and its clients. The position will provide strategic advice regarding product positioning, pricing, promotional activities, digital marketing, Amazon marketplace visibility and distribution channels.  The successful candidate will analyse market and performance information, prepare marketing plans, coordinate campaigns and provide recommendations to help brands strengthen their presence and commercial performance across Amazon and related e-commerce channels.  This is a strategic and analytical marketing position and is not a predominantly sales, graphic design, customer service or advertising production role.   Benefits      Competitive salary plus superannuation.  Full-time professional marketing position.  Exposure to established Australian and international consumer brands.  Opportunities to work across different products and market categories.  Professional development within the Amazon and e-commerce marketing sector.  Supportive and collaborative working environment.  Opportunities for career growth as the business expands.    Task & responsibilities  Key Duties and Responsibilities  The Marketing Specialist will be responsible for:   Developing and implementing marketing strategies, objectives and programs to support the growth of Totalyty and its client brands.  Conducting market and competitor research to identify customer trends, product opportunities and emerging market segments.  Analysing marketplace, sales, customer and campaign data to develop evidence-based marketing recommendations.  Advising clients on product positioning, pricing, promotional strategies, advertising and e-commerce distribution channels.  Preparing marketing plans for product launches, seasonal campaigns, brand expansion and entry into new Amazon marketplaces.  Planning and coordinating integrated marketing campaigns across Amazon, search, social media, email and other digital channels.  Developing strategies for product listing optimisation, keyword positioning, brand presentation and organic search visibility.  Monitoring campaign performance, conversion rates, traffic and advertising expenditure and recommending improvements to maximise return on investment.  Coordinating with clients, creative professionals, content providers and external agencies to implement approved marketing activities.  Preparing marketing briefs, campaign reports, marketplace reviews and strategic recommendations for management and clients.    Qualification & experience  To be considered for this position, applicants should have:   A Bachelor degree or higher qualification in Marketing, Advertising, Business Communications, Public Relations, Commerce or a closely related discipline.  At least two to three years of relevant professional marketing experience.  Demonstrated experience developing and implementing marketing strategies and plans.  Experience conducting market, customer and competitor research.  Strong knowledge of product positioning, pricing, promotion and digital distribution channels.  Experience analysing marketing, sales and campaign performance data.  Knowledge of Amazon, e-commerce marketplaces or online retail environments is highly desirable.  Experience with digital marketing, SEO, sponsored advertising, content optimisation and associated analytics.  Strong commercial judgement and the ability to translate data into practical marketing recommendations.  Excellent written, verbal, presentation and stakeholder-management skills.  The ability to manage multiple client projects, campaigns and deadlines.  Strong attention to detail and the ability to work effectively in a collaborative agency environment.   About Company    Totalyty is a specialist Amazon and e-commerce agency that assists businesses in establishing, managing and growing their brands on Amazon.  We provide end-to-end Amazon marketplace services, including Amazon channel strategy, full-service account management, retail readiness, product listing optimisation, sponsored advertising, promotional planning, Amazon Store development, A+ Content, product imagery and international marketplace expansion.  We work closely with businesses to understand their products, customers and commercial objectives and develop tailored strategies to improve brand visibility, customer engagement, sales conversion and sustainable marketplace growth.      Work Type:  Full time   Salary:  $75000-85000   Job Publish:  24-07-2026   Job Expire:  23-08-2026  Apply on:  Marketing Specialist Job here!    This job is brought to you by workinitiatives.com.au.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Employment Type: Temporary Part Time
Position Classification: Registered Nurse
Remuneration: $40.02 - $56.19 per hour
Hours Per Week: 24
Located in: Gosford Hospital
Requisition ID: REQ662535
Applications Close: Sunday 12th July at 11:59pm

Make a meaningful impact on the future of healthcare by combining your clinical expertise with innovative research.

About the Opportunity

Join our dedicated research team and play a key role in advancing healthcare outcomes through the delivery of high-quality clinical trials while providing exceptional patient-centred care.

In this role you will:

Coordinate and support the delivery of clinical trials in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP), ethical requirements and research governance standards.

Identify, recruit and monitor suitable participants for clinical research studies, ensuring informed consent and participant safety throughout the trial process.

Provide education and support to patients, families and multidisciplinary team members regarding clinical trial participation.

Perform protocol-specific clinical assessments and procedures, including specimen collection, data collection and patient monitoring.

Maintain accurate and timely study documentation, data management and reporting to sponsors, investigators and regulatory bodies.

Collaborate with investigators, sponsors, research governance staff and multidisciplinary teams to ensure the successful delivery of research projects and quality patient outcomes.

For more information about this role, please view the Position Description

About You

We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented clinician who is passionate about research, patient care and contributing to improved health outcomes through the delivery of high-quality clinical trials.

We are looking for someone who has:

Current registration as a Registered Nurse or Registered Midwife with AHPRA, together with relevant clinical research, clinical trials or data management experience.

Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice (ICH-GCP), research governance requirements and ethical principles relating to clinical research.

Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with patients, families, investigators, sponsors and multidisciplinary teams.

Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.

Experience using clinical and administrative systems, including Microsoft Office applications, to manage study data and documentation.

The ability to work both independently and collaboratively, demonstrating sound clinical judgement, accountability and a commitment to quality patient care.

Applicants must have current work rights in Australia or be a permanent resident or citizen. Unfortunately, we cannot consider applicants who do not meet this requirement.

Benefits

Work-Life Balance: Enjoy an accrued day off each month, 17.5% annual leave loading, and paid parental leave.

Financial Benefits: Boost your take-home pay with salary packaging, save on car costs with novated leasing, and access relocation assistance.

Health & Wellbeing: Stay active with discounted gym memberships (Fitness Passport), free flu vaccinations, telehealth support, and confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) counselling for you and your family. Plus, access discounted private health insurance.

Career Growth: Advance your career with free professional development courses and secondment opportunities.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Your Role as Engagement Coordinator

The Engagement Coordinator leads Wesley Mission Queensland's volunteer recruitment and engagement function, ensuring a high-quality, compliant and efficient end-to-end volunteer experience. Working closely with internal stakeholders, this role oversees volunteer attraction, recruitment, onboarding and placement while providing functional leadership to the Engagement Officer.

By driving recruitment strategies, monitoring performance and fostering collaborative partnerships, the Engagement Coordinator plays a key role in building a sustainable volunteer workforce that strengthens our services and communities.

Key responsibilities include:

Leading and supporting the day-to-day activities of the Engagement Officer, providing functional guidance and coaching.

Developing and implementing volunteer recruitment strategies to attract a diverse and sustainable volunteer workforce.

Partnering with service leaders to identify volunteer workforce needs and develop engaging volunteer position descriptions.

Overseeing the end-to-end volunteer recruitment, selection, onboarding and placement process, ensuring all compliance requirements are met.

Acting as the primary point of contact for complex volunteer recruitment enquiries and providing expert advice to internal stakeholders.

Monitoring volunteer recruitment activity, analysing data and reporting on recruitment performance, trends and outcomes.

Driving continuous improvement initiatives to enhance recruitment processes, volunteer engagement and placement success.

Coordinating volunteer recognition initiatives and representing Volunteer Relations at internal and external events.

Building strong relationships with community organisations and stakeholders to promote volunteer opportunities and strengthen volunteer pipelines.

Supporting the Team Leader - Projects with strategic initiatives and other duties as required.

This is a part-time position consisting of 27.5 hours per week.

What We Offer

Community-Focused Team Culture: Be part of a passionate team that values connection, collaboration, and making a genuine difference in people's lives every day.

Salary Packaging: As a not-for-profit employee, you can package up to $15,900 each year on everyday living expenses and up to $2,650 on meals and entertainment, reducing your taxable income and giving you more in your pocket.

Flexibility and Balance: We offer a range of flexible work options to help you achieve the balance that works for you.

Free and Secure Car Parking: Enjoy complimentary access to secure parking while you're at work.

What We're Looking For

Strong understanding of the non-profit sector and the operational requirements of delivering volunteer services in diverse community settings.

Demonstrated expertise in end-to-end recruitment, including multi-channel sourcing, candidate screening and values-aligned interviewing.

Proven ability to lead, mentor and support a small team to achieve high-performance outcomes.

Exceptional interpersonal and stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to influence and build collaborative relationships.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience developing reports, position descriptions and recruitment content.

High-level accuracy in data management, reporting and documentation, ensuring regulatory compliance.

Experience using CRM platforms, Volunteer Management Systems and data to monitor performance and inform decision-making.

A proactive approach to identifying opportunities for continuous improvement and implementing innovative recruitment solutions.

A Valuable Addition, Yet Not a Must-Have!

Tertiary qualification, diploma or equivalent experience in Community Services, Volunteer Management, Human Resources, Administration or a related field.

Comprehensive knowledge of the National Standards for Volunteer Involvement and volunteer lifecycle best practice.

Experience leading volunteer recruitment or workforce engagement programs within the community, aged care or not-for-profit sector.

Essential Requirements

Proof of COVID-19 vaccination status (or as required by legislation and WMQ policy).

Relevant probity checks required by legislation and Wesley Mission Queensland policy.

Current Driver's Licence and willingness to travel as required.

Apply Now!

Lead meaningful volunteer engagement and help shape stronger communities - Click Apply today!

Join a Team Where Your Leadership Makes a Difference

Our Volunteer Relations Team is dedicated to connecting passionate people with meaningful opportunities that strengthen our communities. As the Engagement Coordinator, you'll provide leadership to our volunteer recruitment function, guiding strategy, supporting your team and working alongside service leaders to ensure volunteers are successfully matched, welcomed and supported.

Together, we'll continue building an engaged volunteer workforce that brings Wesley Mission Queensland's mission to life every day.    Click here to Apply now →

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Job Description:

Role title: Clinical Support Officer

Role type: Maximum Term Part-Time (24hrs-week) until December 2026

Role grade: Administrative Officer Level 2, (Year 1-2)

Department and location: Rehabilitation Unit, St Vincent's Hospital, Darlinghurst

Salary: +$66,608- $68,817 (pro-rata) + super + salary package

Better and fairer care. Always.

We are St Vincent's Health Australia, Australia's largest not-for-profit provider of health and aged care services. 

Founded by The Sisters of Charity in 1857, our +30,000 healthcare superheroes operate public and private hospitals, residential aged care, community and virtual care, and outreach programs. 

About the role

Managing roster and HR data entry, including maintaining electronic rosters, processing approved staffing changes and ensuring workforce records are accurate and up to date.

Supporting workforce administration activities such as recruitment, leave management, payroll enquiries, performance review processes and staff replacement coordination.

Assisting with data management and reporting, including preparing workforce, finance and quality reports and providing administrative support for patient care-related activities.

Coordinating ward-unit resources by monitoring stock levels, arranging the purchase and maintenance of equipment, and ensuring supplies are available to support patient care delivery.

Providing comprehensive administrative support to the multidisciplinary healthcare team, including meeting coordination, scheduling activities, organising travel and accommodation, and supporting ward rounds and other operational functions.

About you

Demonstrated experience in administration within a fast-paced environment, with the ability to manage workforce records, rostering and HR data accurately.

Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple priorities and meet deadlines with a high level of attention to detail.

Experience providing administrative support across workforce functions, including recruitment, leave administration, payroll enquiries and staff coordination.

Well-developed computer skills, with experience using Microsoft Office and electronic HR, rostering or patient administration systems to prepare reports and maintain accurate records.

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams while maintaining confidentiality and delivering high-quality customer service.

Why work at St Vincent's?

Join us on our mission to provide care to all, including the most at-risk people in our community

Discounted access to many gyms for you and your family with Fitness Passport

Access to discounted private health insurance with Medibank

Access to a government salary sacrifice program. Make a proportion of your salary tax-free

Committed to financial support for educational development, scholarship programs, paid study leave

About the hospital

In this role you will be based at St Vincent's hospital, Darlinghurst. 

A busy inner-city hospital in a beautiful location

Surrounded by great cafes, galleries and theatres, parks, nightlife, and nearby glorious beaches

A place of expert clinical care for at-risk people

Closely partnered with universities & affiliated research institutes, many of which are located on-campus

Centres of excellence include heart & lung transplantation, bone marrow transplantation, cardiology, cancer care, AIDS-HIV, respiratory medicine, mental health, homeless health, drug & alcohol services, and correctional health 

Sponsorship - work rights for Australi

Please note, visa sponsorship is not available for this position. For this role you must be an Australian or New Zealand citizen or have an Australia visa that grants you the work rights necessary for the role.

Pre-employment checks

Your employment is conditional upon the completion of all role-required pre-employment checks, including relevant immunisations.

Equal opportunity

We celebrate diversity & inclusion and are committed to equal employment opportunity for everyone.

As part of our commitment to reconciliation, we encourage Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples to apply and join us in delivering care that heals body, mind, spirit and community.

How to apply

The closing date for applications is 17 July 2026. Please apply at your earliest convenience as we will be interviewing strong candidates as you apply.

Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter highlighting how your interest, skills, and experience align with each of the things listed in the About You section of this job advert. 

Respectfully, this role is not open to recruitment agencies.

Reconciliation Action Plan:

At St Vincent's we acknowledge the importance of creating a work environment that is welcoming, safe, equitable and inclusive for Aboriginal and-or Torres Strait Islander Employees. As part of our Commitment to Reconciliation and Closing the Gap in employment related outcomes, we encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples.

For further information, visit https:--www.svha.org.au-about-us-reconciliation or get in contact at indigenouscareers@svha.org.au

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     The Group Manager Clinical Risk and National Standards provides leadership and operational support to hospital divisional leaders and quality coordinators to ensure that safe and high quality patient care is consistently delivered, monitored and improved across all Epworth hospital divisions. Reporting to the Group Director, Clinical Governance, this position, as a member of the clinical governance team, is responsible for establishing and improving organisational relationships, systems and processes to support staff and doctors to deliver safe and effective care that results in optimal clinical outcomes. 

The role is specifically responsible for implementing and continuously improving Epworth Health's Clinical Risk Management system, Clinical Practice system , and Accreditation and industry standards programs.

The position will also: 

Participate in the collation and analysis of patient safety, quality and risk information from internal and external sources including benchmark reports

Oversee the internal and external reporting of patient quality and safety information, ensuring Epworth Health meets its obligations.

Work collaboratively with other members of the team to analyse and link clinical risk information with clinical indicators and trended analysis and support clinical improvement priorities across Epworth

Be an active leader and- or member of clinical governance committees and projects, including representing Academic and Medical Services on committees and clinical service improvement activities

Undertake data analysis and report writing, inclusive of Executive and Board level

Provide managerial oversight of the Outcome and Audit team, and undertaking other duties as directed.

Position Description Inherent Requirement

We will review applications as we receive them.

To be successful in this role, you will bring:

Registered Clinician with Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) or eligible for membership of Professional Association for non-registered allied health professions

Experience in leading clinical risk management and clinical practice systems, processes and programs across multiple hospital sites

Demonstrated ability in the development, implementation and evaluation of safety and quality improvement programs in healthcare

Proven ability to engage and influence stakeholders in utilisation of clinical governance systems and processes.

Leadership in accreditation systems and processes

Demonstrated ability to manage competing demands, meet deadlines and respond to change

Highly developed report writing skills, including business cases, executive briefing papers and project plans

Strong organisational and systems thinking skills and attention to detail

Excellent oral and written communication, interpersonal and consultation skills including strong influencing, negotiating and engagement skills with leaders and teams across all levels of the organisation

A comprehensive knowledge of clinical governance, quality improvement methodologies, Australian healthcare industry relevant legislation, industry codes of practice, National Safety and Quality Healthcare Standards (NSQHS) and organisational policy and procedure

Knowledge of and commitment to clinical risk management, best practice and continuous quality improvement

Demonstrated ability to collect and analyse data and prepare reports for a variety of audiences, inclusive of Executive and Board

Awareness of current and emerging trends in improving safety and quality of patient care

Data analysis and process improvement skills

Why Join Epworth?

At Epworth, it's a community.

It's the sense of belonging and being part of an organisation and a team that works to make sure that every patient matters. In addition to this, you will have access to:

Epworth's enhanced Not for Profit status provides the opportunity for employees to salary package up to $15,900 pre-tax annually, plus $2,650 meals and entertainment allowance leading to greater take home pay

Discounted private health insurance

Reduced cost of health services for you and your family at Epworth

The largest educational scholarship program of its kind in Australia!

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds. This includes First Nations peoples, people with disability, mature-age and young job seekers, members of the LGBTIQA+ community, and individuals from all cultural backgrounds. We are committed to providing an equitable, inclusive, and barrier-free recruitment experience for everyone.

If you need support during the application process or would like to discuss reasonable adjustments, we encourage you to let us know what you need to participate fully and confidently. We understand that sharing your needs can feel daunting, so please know that any information you provide will be treated with the utmost confidentiality and respect.

Ready to Make a Difference?

To apply, click the I'm Interested button to attach your CV and cover letter.

For more information about the role, refer to the attached position description or contact Talent on (03) 9426 0606.

Apply now....we have over 8,000 perspectives at Epworth and we're ready to welcome yours!

It is a condition of employment with Epworth HealthCare, subject to reasonable exemptions, that you have had an annual Influenza vaccination, where this is required under Epworth policy.

As a child safe organisation, all successful applicants are required to satisfactorily clear a National Police Check (conducted by Epworth) and may be required to hold a valid employee Working with Children Check (provided by you).

At Epworth, we believe inclusion and diversity are essential to our culture and values. We focus on fairness and opportunity for all - across race, ability, ethnicity, gender, age, sexuality, cultures and beliefs - that reflect the communities we work in. At Epworth, we care. MWSE plays a vital role in its local community through its investment in and operation of the Foundation and Pathways Programs. recovery  design implement and oversee world class energy system conditioning programs including field based and non-field based training practises  oversee the design and implementation of world class strength and power programs  oversee external providers of a wide range of training modalities required for professional level competition including wrestling, Pilates, yoga and additional recovery methods  oversee the design and implementation of world class best practise recovery practises to ensure all athletes are prepared for each training session and competitive match  oversee all elements of NRL sports nutrition programme including implementation of supplement protocols (including monitoring and reporting to relevant peak bodies such as the NRL), game day and travel scenarios  manage all relevant support staff in the performance department including strength and conditioning coaches, sport scientists and dietitians  liaise with medical staff on injured players, rehabilitation programs and return to play pathways  participate in and lead coach education and curriculum development tasks as required  develop effective partnerships with coaching staff and other external bodies as required       ensure maintenance of all MWSE issued equipment, commitment to protection of all private athlete information and MWSE work resources, and adherence to data protection and research guidelines    Qualification & experience   Experience, skills and qualifications   Essential   Minimum of 5 years full-time experience as Head of Performance  Experience in coordinating strength & conditioning services for national and international programs  A qualification at minimum Bachelor’s degree level in strength and conditioning, sports science or related area specialising in the area of physical preparation of elite athletes   Desirable   Experience as a Strength & Conditioning Coach in high level rugby league or equivalent code for a period of 10 years or above  Demonstrated knowledge of physiology and experience with rugby league players  Honours/Masters/Doctorate degree in strength and conditioning, sports science or related area specializing in the area of
